title: Node in-process job queue
context: In-process job queue on node:events. Up to `concurrency` jobs run at once and jobs start in the order they were added. Each job function returns a promise and gets at most 3 attempts in total; after the last failure the queue emits "failed" with the error, otherwise "done" with the job's result. drain() resolves once nothing is pending or running, and may be called many times over the queue's life.

expected.why: pop takes the newest job (LIFO); jobs must start in insertion order, so this must be shift
the promise is not awaited, so rejections escape the try/catch (no retry, unhandled rejection) and "done" is emitted with a pending promise
attempts is already incremented, so <= 3 re-queues after the third failure and allows a fourth attempt
on() keeps every resolve listener forever; repeated drain() calls leak listeners (MaxListenersExceededWarning); use once()
